title: Publication gate and remaining uncertainty
detail: 172 entries have an approved name, venue and San Francisco geography; 79 candidates are held off the directory. Every unapproved field is blank. A listed entry is not a claim that every fact is known.

title: Dates are a fixed snapshot, not a live calendar
detail: Only approved ISO occurrences determine temporal labels relative to 18 October 2026. Yearless dates (Menorah, Cole Valley Nights, Taraval and others) are never promoted to upcoming dates. A 2027 banner does not date unrelated ancillary events; past editions are not moved forward.

title: Regional and cross-boundary programmes quarantined
detail: Frameline, SF Art Week, SF Climate Week, NEXUS, Bay Area Dance Week, SF Beer Week, the Jewish Film Festival and the full SF Marathon require SF-only components/route evidence. This is not a finding that those events do not exist.

title: Known corrections and conflicts
detail: Zoo resident day is October 7 (not a monthly first-Tuesday rule); Boo October 31 is 10am–3pm with paid admission/membership. Fiesta en el Parque is August 1. Opera Ball moved to November 12. Bhangra & Beats moved to Yerba Buena. Alemany hours, Secondhand/Muertos street extents and Jewish Film Festival year conflict remain flagged, not guessed. Nihonmachi’s 2027 venue is blank: its Japantown reference is in the prior-edition recap, not the future announcement.

title: Concurrent research retained; Ferry Fest dead URL is historical only
detail: The f1fd3c36 audit and 99662c40 repair are preserved unchanged as candidate history, including Alemany Flea Market and Doc Stories. Newly located sources were independently re-read where possible; old field/page labels are not automatic approvals. Ferry Fest’s former https://www.ferrybuildingmarketplace.com/events/ferry-fest/ returned 404 in upstream CI run 39092990628 and is not active evidence. Its surviving SF Travel guide remains a review link; unsupported facts remain blank.

title: Evidence and coverage limitations
detail: HTTP 200, a page title, a name match, a URL year, free parking, free refreshments, and an organization's domain suffix do not establish event facts, admission or nonprofit status. Blank cells are unverified. Commercial ticketing/JS pages, neighborhood micro-events, civic and faith calendars, sports fixtures and individual arts performances need further coverage. No claim of citywide completeness or ongoing automated fact verification is made.

title: Gaming, music and AI research pass (session 3adf31d9)
detail: 15 entries were added from official organizer, venue, library and conference pages: GDC Festival of Gaming; the San Francisco Scholastic Chess Championship and Mechanics' Institute chess programmes; San Francisco Public Library chess, board-game and Chinese-chess clubs; the AI Engineer World's Fair, TDX, ICLR, Data + AI Summit and AI Council conferences; and the Stern Grove Festival. Every value is quoted from the page that was read on 18 October 2026. Where a page states no admission, the price cell is blank and labelled 'Not stated' — never 'Free'. Two candidates are held for review because the captured official text names no venue (Mechanics' Institute Introduction to Chess) or no venue at all (AI Council 2027). Several sources were read through the workspace search tool's verbatim result text rather than a full page fetch (sfpl.org's branch navigation and the Stern Grove contact block); those captures record no HTTP status and are labelled as such.

title: Topic tags and cost badges are labels, not verified fields
detail: The Gaming / Music / AI & technology tags are editorial presentation labels derived from the verified event name (or from this session's explicit decision). A tag never changes a fact, a date or a source, and it is not evidence that an event belongs to a genre. The Free / Paid / Not stated badge is computed only from the verified admission text quoted from the official page, and the exact official wording is always shown next to the badge. A blank admission cell is 'Not stated', never 'Free'.

title: Free-first research pass (session 21f3dd85)
detail: 8 entries were added from official organizer, venue, library and government pages, free gaming/music/AI first: Noontime Concerts (free weekly classical series with three dated Tuesday concerts), the National Park Service Sea Chantey Sing (free, monthly, dated 5 December 2026), the Mechanics' Institute Chess Socials (free, monthly), gaming tournaments at the San Francisco Public Library's Mix teen space (monthly), and the library's annual Tech Week (free workshops including AI sessions). One paid gaming entry — the Mechanics' Institute 2026 Winter Tuesday Night Marathon chess tournament ($70 members / $100 non-members, 3 November to 15 December 2026) — was collected for the separate Paid section. Every value is quoted from the page read on 18 October 2026; where a page states no time or date, the cell stays blank. The Mechanics' Institute chess-classes page lists Chess Socials dates ('Nov 6, Dec 4') without a year, so no ISO occurrence was approved from that list.

title: SFPL admission judgment, two holds, and evidence for a held chess class
detail: For its two new San Francisco Public Library rows this session quotes the library's official events index — 'All programs and events are free and open to the public.' (sfpl.org/events) — as admission evidence, applying that explicit all-programmes statement in context. The seven SFPL gaming rows added by session 3adf31d9 did not cite the index statement, so their admission cells stay blank ('Not stated'); no earlier row was edited, and the visible inconsistency is flagged for a future harmonization decision. Two candidates are held for review: the Internet Archive's Friday public tours (schedule, time, venue and free admission are all confirmed on archive.org, but the page gives the programme no title, and this register requires an approved event name), and Grace Cathedral's Organ Recital Series (official pages conflict — 'Cost: Free' and 'free organ recital' on some recital pages versus a Sunday visitor admission fee unless registered in advance on another, with no price on the fetched series page). Separately, the Mechanics' Institute chess-classes page now states a venue ('Onsite in the Chess Room at Mechanics'') and member pricing for the held 'Introduction to Chess' candidate; that evidence is recorded in data/research/audit-21f3dd85.md for a future corrections pass rather than published as a duplicate row.

title: Free-first gap research pass (session d57e2eeb)
detail: 21 entries were added from official operator, venue, government and community pages read on 18 October 2026: the Cable Car Museum, Randall Museum, San Francisco Railway Museum, Fort Point NHS, Presidio Officers' Club free exhibitions and Musée Mécanique; the Golden Gate Park gardens' free hours (Japanese Tea Garden M/W/F hour, Conservatory of Flowers free first Tuesdays, Botanical Garden daily early entry and free second Tuesdays); free music beyond the big festivals (weekly Noontime Concerts at Old St. Mary's, Grace Cathedral free Choral Evensong, the annual People in Plazas series); gaming additions (Gamescape's weekly Board Game Night, plus Musée Mécanique); recurring SF AI/tech community channels (AI Tinkerers SF, The AI Collective SF chapter, Noisebridge's Circuit Hacking Mondays and monthly Five Minutes of Fame); the free SF Shakespeare Festival parks season, Circus Bella's free Union Square juggling lessons, and the 2026 Bay Area Science Festival at UCSF Mission Bay. One explicitly paid event — Circus Bella's BRAVURA Big Top — is published with a Paid badge, kept distinct from the free-first entries. Every value is quoted from the archived page text; blank cells stay blank and are labelled 'Not stated'. Six irregularities found on official pages themselves (conflicting season-closing and tour dates at circusbella.org, a stale next-event link and year mix-up on the Noisebridge wiki, a year-less upcoming listing on aicollective.com, two-digit years on gamescapesf.store, and Grace Cathedral's free service vs paid sightseeing) are quoted verbatim and flagged on the rows rather than silently reconciled. Five pages were read through the workspace search tool's verbatim result text rather than a direct fetch (museemecanique.com, streetcar.org/museum, gamescapesf.com, gracecathedral.org/calendar-events, ucsf.edu news); those captures record no HTTP status and are labelled as such.
